supersedes_conclusion_in.claim_now_false: root_cause_found_20260918.not_fixable_in_code stated 'The evaluation apparatus is sound' and next_step stated 'No further code change is required.'
supersedes_conclusion_in.what_holds: The expired-credential diagnosis was correct and complete as an explanation of the seven stalled attempts. The source credential was re-authenticated on 2026-09-18T20:16Z and the access token now expires 2026-09-28T20:16Z.
supersedes_conclusion_in.what_does_not_hold: A code change was required. With a valid credential the launch path still resolved a bare-Codex baseline for the OpenCode control, so the lane could not have produced a clean control measurement even once auth was fixed. The credential was the reason nothing ran; it was not the only reason nothing correct would have come out.

finding.summary: Asked to resolve a baseline for profile runtime-opencode-codex-product-v1, the runner returned baseline-fastify-20260822-p-dc16afea3ad5-r2 -- a bare-Codex session on codex-cli. Launching the OpenCode control would have bound it to that session through interpretation.comparison_baseline_session_id and published an OpenCode-versus-Codex-CLI comparison.
finding.why_it_survived_the_previous_repair: Commit 2b9fda77 fixed the condition layer only. resolve_condition_pair stopped pairing an OpenCode condition against a Codex baseline condition, and baseline_descriptor began building an OpenCode control descriptor. Two layers below it kept the retired premise.

layers_still_carrying_it.protocol_builder: refresh_workflow_contracts.frozen_protocol resolved baseline_profile_id to baseline-bare-codex for any non-Claude runtime, under a comment reading 'OpenCode has no baseline of its own: it runs on the Codex subscription and is compared with the bare Codex baseline'. A bare-OpenCode control protocol therefore declared bare Codex as its baseline and the OpenCode control as the treatment.
layers_still_carrying_it.session_layer: run_codex_workflow_evaluation.find_comparison_baseline_record fell the control through to find_canonical_baseline_record, and _run_one_locked hardcoded standalone_opencode_control = False so the control passed the treatment gate and required a reusable baseline of another runtime to exist before it could run.

finding.measurement_consequence: An OpenCode lane read against a bare-Codex control is a statement about the Codex CLI, not about OpenCode. The two share an OpenAI subscription, not a runtime.
finding.operational_consequence: It also coupled the two apparatus, which is what broke the lane on 2026-09-16: raising OpenCode's per-task timeout made the arms disagree on runtime.timeout_seconds_per_task and repository validation correctly refused the pair.

repair.runtime_control_concept: RUNTIME_CONTROL_PROFILE_IDS names every bare-runtime control -- a profile that is its own baseline, passes no treatment gate, binds no comparison baseline, and publishes no comparison record.
repair.deliberately_distinct_set: PRIMARY_OBJECTIVE_BASELINE_PROFILE_IDS still holds only baseline-bare-codex and baseline-claude-code-no-mcp and still decides interpretation.primary_objective_hard_baseline, which the retained OpenCode controls record false.
repair.pool_anchoring: find_pool_profile_record anchored a profile's pool on whatever find_comparison_baseline_record returned, so the borrowed Codex anchor was also what stopped a drifted live descriptor from making a retained session invisible and freeing its replicate slot. The control now anchors on itself through find_pool_control_record, preserving that protection without borrowing another runtime's fingerprint.
repair.unchanged_by_design: The Codex and Claude Code paths are byte-identical. Only the OpenCode branch moved.
repair.validator_already_agreed: validate_repository.py already exempted a standalone OpenCode control from the comparison-binding requirement in both of its checks. The validator was built for this; the runner and the protocol builder were not.
repair.test_isolation_note: The protocol-shape test runs in a subprocess: configure_model_condition patches module-level globals irreversibly and leaked the OpenCode condition into three later tests when called in-process.

retained_evidence_untouched.disposition: Frozen evidence. All four carry a comparison_baseline_session_id naming a bare-Codex session and are filed under the Codex pool fingerprints dc16afea3ad5 and c86863838e8b. They are not rewritten. The 2026-09-16 adapter re-pin already bars pooling them with any run made after that date.
retained_evidence_untouched.protocols: The four existing runtime-opencode-codex-product-v1 protocols all declare bare Codex as baseline and the control as treatment. They keep their bytes and their identities; the corrected descriptor mints new ones.

post_repair_state.required_checks: make check green: 336 tests, repository validation passed, no working-tree churn.

launch.authority: experiment-owner direction on 2026-09-18 to get the OpenCode baseline running, and to treat any OpenCode-to-Codex coupling as a defect to be reverted
launch.replicate_index_rationale: The new pool starts at r2 so the 2026-09-16 adapter re-pin is visible in the index, per the restoration receipt.
launch.credential_verified_in_lane: The lane-private OpenCode credential materialized from the re-authenticated source and expires 2026-09-28T20:16:04Z. The stale lane copies under /opt/data/eval-codex-homes expired 2026-08-29 and belong to the older fixture path, not the workflow lane path, which builds a fresh home per session.

new_pool_fingerprints.note: OpenCode's own pool, not the Codex dc16afea3ad5 the retained controls were filed under.
